set_aside.subject: K-02 function purity guarantee
set_aside.text: “no clock, no randomness” and “it is no guarantee against code written to get around it”
set_aside.question: Is absence of clock and randomness a guaranteed property of every admitted function, or may an admitted function deliberately obtain time or random data despite still being called pure?
options: Guarantee the property and refuse any implementation that can obtain either source
Guarantee only interception of specified standard-library calls and permit undetected circumvention
Stop describing admitted functions as unconditionally having no clock or randomness
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the stated sandbox boundary as a guarantee and refuse circumvention.

witness.initial: A contract has a nonempty passing corpus, and its submitted implementation deliberately obtains the current time without calling an intercepted standard-library entry point.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The owner or agent later runs a flow containing the admitted implementation at two different times.
outcomes: The implementation is refused because an admitted function must have no clock.
The implementation is admitted because the stated guard covers only ordinary standard-library entry points; the two runs can produce different outputs from equal declared inputs.
witness.observer: The owner or agent inspecting the admission verdict, run outputs and traces

set_aside.subject: Clock and randomness interception boundary
set_aside.text: “the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: Which Python standard-library entry points, indirect calls and nondeterministic facilities count as clock or randomness sources that the sandbox must withhold?
options: An exhaustive named set of APIs such as time, datetime, random, secrets, uuid and os entropy entry points
Only direct calls to selected clock and pseudorandom APIs
All direct and indirect standard-library paths that can expose time, entropy or nondeterministic values
set_aside.default_guess: Define and intercept an exhaustive named set, including indirect standard-library paths to those sources.

witness.initial: A valid implementation calls datetime.datetime.now(), while another calls random.SystemRandom().randint(); neither calls time.time() or random.random().
events: An agent submits both implementations for trial and admission.
The sandbox applies its interpretation of “standard library's own entry points”.
outcomes: Both calls are withheld because datetime and SystemRandom are covered clock and randomness entry points.
One or both calls execute because the implementation intercepts only a narrower set of direct APIs.
witness.observer: The agent sees different trial evidence and admission verdicts; later callers may see nondeterministic outputs

set_aside.subject: Observable result of withholding clock or randomness
set_aside.text: “The clock and randomness are withheld from a function that calls the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: What observable result must occur when a function invokes a withheld entry point, in both trials and real runs, and how is it classified?
options: Terminate execution as a sandbox violation
Make the API unavailable or raise an exception that function code may catch
set_aside.default_guess: Terminate the execution and record a sandbox violation.

witness.initial: A submitted implementation calls time.time() inside a try/except and would return a declared fallback value if the call raises.
events: An agent requests a trial of the implementation.
outcomes: The sandbox terminates the trial and reports sandbox violation, so the fallback cannot run.
The call raises an ordinary catchable exception, the function returns its fallback, and the case may pass and be admitted.
witness.observer: The agent inspecting trial evidence and the resulting admission verdict
